title: Throughput Stabilizer: adaptive batching recommender with safe reversion
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Build an automated recommender and safe-apply pipeline that adjusts batching and KV-cache settings per-route to reduce unit cost while preserving latency and throughput SLOs. The system must (1) propose candidate config deltas, (2) dry-run via shadow evaluation and simulated load, (3) apply changes gradually to production with SLO-aware routing and limiters, and (4) reliably roll back / partially revert on anomalies.

Context: We have many existing tuning projects but still rely on manual tuning or heavy conservatism. This ticket unifies a recommender engine, canary/staged apply orchestration, and an anomaly detector that triggers deterministic rollback. Target customers: hosted API routes with mixed latency profiles, Dedicated customers with strict throughput contracts, and Private deployments where operators want automated suggestions but safe defaults.

Goals: Reduce token cost per request by 12-25% on targeted routes without violating per-route latency SLOs (p99 <= configured SLO). Provide a fully automated safe-apply path that can be configured by product teams with policy knobs (aggressiveness, traffic fraction, revert thresholds).

Approach:
- Recommender: offline analysis of per-route token distribution, input length histograms, KV cache hit-rate, and existing batch window utilization. Generate candidate profiles (batch size, max-concurrency, prefetch horizon, cache TTL, quantization profile) and rank by estimated cost savings and expected latency delta.
- Dry-run: run candidates in shadow mode for 24h on 2-5% sampled traffic; collect simulated token throughput, tail-latency delta, error-rate change. Use deterministic simulator that replays requests against candidate config on a staging fleet to estimate kernel-level latency.
- Staged apply: ramp plan with steps 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% using canary window durations configurable per-route (default 5m for small steps, 30m for >20%).
- Limiters: per-route concurrency cap, global token-rate budget, and CPU/GPU utilization thresholds. If limiters are hit, the orchestrator pauses ramp and either reduces batch aggressiveness or routes newly arriving traffic to fallback model variant.
- SLO-aware routing: if a route's observed metrics approach its SLO boundary (p99 >= SLO * 0.95 or error rate growing), route a fraction of traffic to a more conservative runtime variant (smaller batch, stronger prefetch, or prior config). Routing decisions use per-route EWMA to avoid oscillation.
- Anomaly detection and rollback: multilayered detectors (fast detector: 2-minute sliding window, slow detector: 30-minute trend) looking at p99, p95 skew, error rate, and KPI regressions (token-per-second and successful responses). Rollback triggers: p99 > SLO + 15% for 2m OR error-rate increase >= 2x baseline sustained for 5m OR sudden drop in success throughput > 10% within 2m. Rollback actions include: immediate full rollback to last known-good config, partial rollback of batch size only, or slow-stepped reduction of aggressiveness with a hold period. Every automatic rollback must create an incident artifact with diffs and metrics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Recommender produces ranked candidates with expected cost delta and estimated latency delta for >90% of routes.
- Shadow/dry-run predicts real production impact within +/- 12% on p95/p99 for tested routes.
- Safe-apply pipeline can ramp a config to 50% traffic with no customer-facing SLO violations on 95% of runs in internal canary experiments.
- Automated rollback detects and reverts regressions within 5 minutes on fast detectors and creates a reproducible incident.

Key metrics to track: p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate (5xx/timeout), per-request token cost, successful RPS, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, rollback frequency, time-to-detect, time-to-recover.

Operator controls (UI/API): toggle aggressiveness, set route SLOs, whitelist/blacklist routes from automation, set max daily cost-savings quota, enable/disable auto-rollback.

Security/Compliance: The system must never send customer payloads outside configured VPCs for Private deployments during dry-run. Audit logs must capture every config diff and every rollout step.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ranked candidate list produced for target routes with estimated cost and latency impact (string fields saved in candidate artifact). 2) Shadow run error between predicted and observed p95/p99 <= 12% on evaluation set. 3) No more than 0.1% of total production requests experience SLO breach during staged ramps across internal canary runs. 4) Automated rollback executes within configured windows and leaves a clear audit trail.
updates: 2025-11-05 - Maya Chen: Initial scoping done. Collected dataset exports for last 90 days (token histograms, p99 per-route), stored at gs://redwood-ops/optim/ENG-30211/inputs.zip.

2025-11-09 - Rafael Ortiz: Prototype recommender produced candidate set for 30 high-traffic routes. Preliminary estimator shows median predicted cost reduction of 14% with expected p99 increase of 3-8ms.
2025-11-12 - QA Lead Priya Singh: Shadow harness ready; requesting small fleet allocation for simulated runs. We need a staging GPU pool (2x A100) for kernel latency replay.
2025-11-15 - Rafael Ortiz: Implemented fast-detector (2m window) and rollback orchestration. Integration tests show rollback executed end-to-end in 45s in staging when simulating 2x error-rate spike.

2025-11-18 - PM review (Diego Alvarez): Reviewed roll-forward policy. Asked to add a graded revert option that reduces batch by 25% before full revert to minimize sudden cost regressions. Rafael to add this by 2025-11-25.
notes: Trade-offs considered: conservative ramps reduce cost capture speed; aggressive approaches increase rollback frequency and incident noise. We plan a two-track rollout: conservative autopilot for Tier-1 routes (low aggressiveness, longer hold times) and an experimental aggressive mode for internal non-customer-facing routes to validate headroom. Ops will have a manual override and a one-click revert in Console. Future: integrate with Optimize to suggest quantization profiles per-model during recommendation cycle.
followups: Post-ship: add ML model to score candidate stability using historical rollback traces (Q1 2026)
Add per-customer policy layer for Dedicated customers to disable automation at org level
